Stress-tolerant Rice Varieties
Product Catalogue - South Asia

Sahbhagi Dhan / BRRI Dhan 56 / Sukha Dhan 3 (IR 74371-70-1-1-CRR-1)
Salient features: Released in 2009 and notified in 2011, Sahbhagi Dhan is a conventionally bred drought-tolerant variety for commercial cultivation in India, Nepal (Sukha Dhan 3) and Bangladesh (BRRI Dhan 56). It has the potential to yield well under drought conditions due to its ability to have better grain setting under drought.
Parent variety: IR 55419-4*2/WAY RAREM
Duration in days: 105-110
Suitable land type: Upland and upper shallow
lowland

IR64-Drt1 (DRR 42, IR 87707-445-B-B-B-RP 5208-3; IET 22836)
Salient features: DRR 42 is the improved version of another popular variety IR 64 developed through marker assisted breeding. Along with drought-tolerance potential, it has an added advantage of high yield production. Tolerant to drought, especially drought at flowering and grain filling stage. Resistant to blast, moderately resistant to bacterial blight, brown spot.

Swarna Shreya (IET 24003) (RCPR-8-IR 84899-B-179-16-1-1-1)
Salient features: Swarna Shreya is a high yielding, semi-dwarf, early maturity rice variety suitable for cultivation in aerobic condition or water limiting areas in Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar states. It is moderately resistant to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, sheath rot and RTD diseases. It also showed moderately resistance to major pests like stem borer, leaf folder, gall midge (biotype 1) and whorl maggot under natural screening.
Parent variety: IR 78877-208-B-1-1 / IRRI 132
Year of notification: 2016
Duration in days: 120-125

metadata.section: Stress-tolerant Rice for Africa and South Asia (STRASA)

chunks.text:
About STRASA:
Since 2007, IRRI's project Stress-Tolerant Rice for Africa and South Asia (STRASA) in collaboration with AfricaRice delivered rice varieties tolerant to abiotic stresses benefitting nearly 18 million farmers in South Asia and Sub-Sahara cultivating rice in unfavourable environments.
Supported by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, it is a collaborative effort to develop and deliver highyield rice varieties tolerant to abiotic stresses;
submergence, drought, and salinity in South Asia and submergence, drought, salinity, cold and iron toxicity in Africa.
Now in its final phase of implementation ending in 2019, the project aims to reduce poverty and hunger, and increase food and income security for resourcepoor farm families and rice consumers in South Asia and Sub-Sahara Africa through the development and dissemination of high-yield rice varieties tolerant to abiotic stresses.
Suitable land type: Medium shallow lowland
Grain type: Short bold Plant height: 80-98 cm
Yield: 5-5.5 t/ha
